newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: JG Summit 9-mth profits helped by units.
newsitem.headline: JG Summit 9-mth profits helped by units.

text.p: JG Summit Holdings Inc, the diversified holding company of Filipino-Chinese tycoon John Gokongwei, said on Thursday its nine-month profits largely came from two banking affiliates and real estate arm.
It reported that its nine-month net profits on a recurring basis rose by 8.5 percent in the January to September period to 2.20 billion pesos from the year-earlier 2.03 billion pesos.
Revenues increased by 26 percent to 12.99 billion from 10.28 billion pesos.

Including extraordinary gains of 1.92 billion pesos from the sale of its equity in a bank, net profits totalled 4.13 billion pesos for the nine-month period, an increase of 103 percent from last year, the company said.
Its banking affiliates reported improved interest income from strong loan growth, the company said.

Far East Bank and Trust Co, 19 percent-owned by J.G. Summit, logged a 23 percent increase in net income to 1.65 billion pesos in the first nine months compared with 1.34 billion pesos in the same period last year, JG Summit said.
Philippine Commercial International Bank, in which JG Summit has a 14.24 percent stake, had a 22 percent hike in net income to 2.17 billion pesos from 1.78 billion pesos.
JG Summit's property firm, Robinson's Land Corp, churned out net profits of 404.4 million pesos in the nine months ending June 30, up 91 percent from 211.5 million pesos in the same period in 1995.
The growth in Robinson's Land's earnings was due to improved revenues from shopping center and hotel operations, JG Summit said.
Its food unit, Universal Robina Corp., had a 4.5 percent increase in net profit to 930.8 million pesos for the nine months ending June 30 from 890.4 million pesos in the like-period last year.
